A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Jasmine, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Renamed components and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI and zero-shot depth-estimation results, component ablations, auxiliary-image experiments, and qualitative evaluations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds improved-ground-truth KITTI evaluation, computational measurements, depth-distribution analysis, and training-stability results.

M1.justification: The single-step SD model, reconstruction surrogate, two-iteration SSG, teacher and auxiliary losses, and staged freezing remain. HIR is renamed MIR, while the explicit SSG update and training pseudocode document the existing procedure. The freezing schedule moves to Appendix H.

E1.justification: Both versions use KITTI, Hypersim, CityScape, DrivingStereo weather conditions, ETH3D, and Virtual KITTI for the same purposes. The improved-KITTI-ground-truth evaluation changes the evaluation protocol without establishing a new domain or task. Additional application domains appear only as future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds Marigold to the existing KITTI and zero-shot comparisons in Tables 1–2; v1's SD comparator group contained E2E FT and Lotus. The existing self-supervised comparators and supplementary stereo/multi-frame comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation using improved KITTI ground truth, MAC/runtime profiling at 1024×320 on an RTX 4090, and a training comparison jointly disabling teacher supervision and multistage freezing. Existing splits, preprocessing, training budget, and alignment assignments remain unchanged; Section 4.3 explains previously used alignment procedures.

E4.justification: New Figure 4(b) examines depth distributions across SSG iterations, Appendix H/Figure 9 tests training stability with a joint teacher/freezing ablation, and Section 4.5 profiles computational cost. These substantially extend supporting analysis beyond the retained component, auxiliary-image, reconstruction-ratio, and qualitative loss ablations.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 Figure 9 introduces error bars and states that multiple training runs were examined after 25k steps. Run counts, seeds, and the statistical meaning of the bars remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, but v2 adds Marigold results, improved-GT Table 5, latency/MAC results, and distribution/stability findings. Jasmine's new improved-GT AbsRel of 0.061 is under different ground truth from the retained 0.090 raw-GT result. Figure 9 reports 9.00% versus 10.54% AbsRel for Jasmine and the joint ablation. Table 2 removes previously reported SqRel and a2 entries.

T1.justification: The scale-invariance argument and Appendix A derivation are retained. GRU equations move to Appendix D, and the explicit affine SSG update restates the operation already depicted in v1. Standard formulas explaining the existing alignment procedures introduce no new theorem or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about the first SD-based self-supervised framework, prior preservation, SSG alignment, KITTI performance, and generalization remain. v2's introduction additionally presents bridging self-supervised and zero-shot evaluation and analyzing depth de-normalization as contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 substantially interprets alignment-dependent scores through outlier sensitivity, metric behavior, comparison fairness, and in-domain versus zero-shot suitability. Section 4.5 discusses computational tradeoffs, and Appendix I explicitly identifies driving-only primary training as a limitation. These materially expand interpretation beyond v1's brief alignment disclosure and general scaling discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds a detailed workflow and Algorithm 1, including task-switch codes and timestep 999; Section 3.2 explains conditioning through time embeddings. v2 also supplies a project/code link and inference-profiling hardware. Conversely, Table 4 removes the comparator-specific resolutions disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual references for metric depth, GRU-based depth estimation, improved KITTI ground truth, and potential completion/super-resolution/MVS applications. It clarifies that earlier self-supervised diffusion methods used their own diffusion models and removes the SQLdepth-exclusion discussion. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes method exposition and the supplement: HIR becomes MIR, GRU equations and freezing details move to appendices, and stepwise explanations and pseudocode are introduced. The appendix gains a contents list and structured subsections, while references move before it. These changes extend beyond inserting experimental results.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Pipeline and method figures are redrawn or rearranged, Table 2 becomes a cross-dataset matrix, and new distribution, alignment, uncertainty, improved-GT, and latency displays appear. Existing qualitative comparison images are retained and rescaled.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens supporting evidence through Marigold comparisons, improved-GT evaluation, and mechanism/stability analyses, while clarifying training and alignment-dependent evaluation and documenting computational cost. The gains are limited by unspecified error-bar construction and run counts, plus removal of Table 2 metrics and Table 4 resolutions. Overall, these additions provide a useful but bounded quality improvement to the retained scientific contribution.
